title: The freshness rule, `engram backup status`, the doctor block and the `next` reminder
outcome: The freshness rule, `engram backup status`, the doctor block and the `next` reminder
acceptance: One pure function takes the configuration, the recorded state, the running build's format identities and the clock and returns, per kind, either qualifying or exactly one reason, the first that applies in the order of the brief's table; a table test produces `local_backed_up` and each of `backup_record_unreadable`, `backup_not_configured`, `backup_never_confirmed`, `backup_target_changed`, `backup_other_format`, `backup_clock_invalid`, `backup_copy_missing`, `backup_confirmation_expired` and `backup_stale`, including a future timestamp, an old store copy on an unchanged store confirmed a minute ago (stale), and a copy whose confirmation and capture are both older than the window (confirmation expired)

`engram backup status [--json]` reads only local files and the store: it prints the mode and, for each qualifying kind, its off-host text and what it restores, then per configured kind the acknowledgement, who made the assertion and when, the capture start and age, the cut and how far the store has moved, the last confirmation, the checking build when it differs from the running one, a pending attempt, and the last attempt with its error; an unreadable configuration or state file is reported as the typed reason `backup_record_unreadable` and not as a crash; the `--json` receipt carries a schema version; a test asserts that no output prints the mode without the off-host field and that a directory target reads exactly "off-host asserted; not verified"

`engram backup status --check-target` asks the adapter to confirm under a deadline: a copy the target no longer holds is recorded and reads `backup_copy_missing` at once; an unreachable target is reported as `backup_target_unreachable`, and a check that reached the target and passed its deadline before it had read the copy as `backup_check_timed_out`, each beside the recorded evidence without changing it; `engram doctor` prints the same block in text and JSON from the recorded evidence, apart from store health, and contacts no target: a test with an adapter that fails every request shows doctor's backup block and exit unchanged, and a test shows a stale or missing backup leaves a healthy store's `healthy` value true

A check records its result only under the push lock and only when the newest receipt is still the one it checked; a test lets a push record a newer receipt between the check's read and its write and shows the check record nothing

`next` and `next --peek` add one reminder line when a target is configured and the mode is `local`, or when the last attempt failed, and add nothing when no target is configured or all is well; they read only the recorded state; tests cover the four cases and that a failed last attempt shows while an earlier copy still qualifies

A test moves the clock past the window with no new push and shows the mode change from `local_backed_up` to `local` with `backup_confirmation_expired`; after `status --check-target` then confirms that old copy without a new capture, the reason reads `backup_stale`

This changeset adds no backup-dependent field, health value or admission change to `engram readiness --json`, and a test asserts readiness output is the same with and without a configured target; docs/shipped.md and docs/features/cli-and-mcp.md describe the status word, the doctor block and the reminder
